verdict: The copy is specific, honest and sounds like the feed it sells into: the hero pair, the Try box microcopy, the 'Never.' list and the pricing lines are best-in-class, with no banned words, no invented proof, every heading at two lines and the phone budget met (9.96 screens at 390, 9.70 at 360). It stops short of 9.5 because the visitor's own-line result oversells on the lead audience's most common drafts (hedged crypto calls keep their hedges under a 'Why it hits' label), plus a handful of small copy and state slips.
to_95: Make the Try box result honest about light edits: when only filler words were cut and hedges such as 'i think', 'might', 'In my opinion' or 'not financial advice but' remain, swap the 'Why it hits' label for 'What changed' and add one line pointing at the remaining hedge ('Still hedged: "i think" and "might" are your call. Tap either to cut it.') or at the in-app rewrite.
Stop the Why line from quoting the whole result back ('It now opens on "We just raised $2M to help creators grow"'): quote the first three or four words only.
Clear the stale 'Your line' in the signup sheet (and the hidden 'Sharpened:' text) once the visitor clears the box or loads an example.
Trim the pricing footnote to one line of rewrite maths and move the rest behind 'See everything included'.

issues.where: Your facts stay / The fluff goes: result for a visitor's own hedged line, e.g. 'gm. i think $SOL might possibly go higher this week tbh' -> 'gm. i think $SOL might go higher this week.'; 'honestly not financial advice but i'm long eth at 3,100' -> 'not financial advice but i'm long eth at 3,100.'; 'In my opinion, I really think that most founders should probably...' -> 'In my opinion, most founders should...'
issues.problem: For the lead audience (crypto and trading writers) the most common draft is a hedged call. The demo strikes the filler but leaves the loudest hedges, then heads the explanation 'Why it hits' and says 'The line says the same without them', followed by 'Keep it. Start free'. The result does not hit, so the label oversells and the visitor's first personal proof reads weaker than the curated examples.
issues.fix: When the edit only removed filler and hedge words remain, change the label to 'What changed', keep the current sentence, and add one line: 'Still hedged: "i think" and "might" are yours to keep or cut.' (or mark them as tappable optional cuts). Keep 'Why it hits' for moves that restructure the line (split, number first, said it straight).

issues.where: Result for 'Excited to announce that we just raised $2M to help creators grow'
issues.problem: The Why line quotes the entire sharpened line back: 'It now opens on "We just raised $2M to help creators grow", not the run-up to it.' It reads machine-made directly under the same sentence.
issues.fix: Quote only the opening words: 'It now opens on "We just raised $2M", not the run-up to it.' Cap the quote at four words whenever the frame cut leaves the whole line.

issues.where: Start free sheet after the visitor clears the Try box or loads an example chip
issues.problem: The sheet still shows 'Your line: thread: why 90% of traders lose money.' after that line was cleared and an example was loaded; the hidden 'Sharpened:' status text also stays stale after Clear.
issues.fix: Drop the 'Your line' row and reset the hidden status text when the box is cleared or an example is showing; show it only for the visitor's current own line.

issues.where: Three-line footnote under the plan cards
issues.problem: 'A rewrite is three takes on a line. Ten reply drafts use one. Learning your voice uses 5, once. Answers drafted for Pro's reply pings use none.' is four accounting rules at the moment of choosing a plan; it makes a simple offer feel metered.
issues.fix: Keep 'A rewrite is three takes on a line.' and 'Cancel anytime: a yearly plan runs to the end of its year.' on the page; move the other three rules into 'See everything included'.

issues.where: Free card, first bullet under the heading 'Sharpening is free. Forever.'
issues.problem: The first thing under the boldest promise is its caveat ('Past a daily fair-use limit, a lighter check runs on your device. Still free.'), in the largest sub-line on the card.
issues.fix: Keep it truthful but lead with the promise: 'Sharpen every line you write' then the shorter variant already in the markup, 'Past fair use: a lighter check, still free.', at all widths.

issues.where: It learns how you write: 'You put it back once. Once more and it stays.'
issues.problem: The line describes an action the visitor has not taken yet, so the first read is confusing until they press 'Put it back'.
issues.fix: Start state: 'Put "ngl" back twice and it stays for good.' Switch to 'You put it back once. Once more and it stays.' only after the first press.
